name: Avalanche Confirmed-State Latency Experiment
description: This software project provides a complete reproducible framework for studying confirmed-state access latency in a permissioned Avalanche Layer-1 blockchain network. The project accompanies the research study “A Blockchain Solution for Reducing Confirmed-State Access Latency in an Avalanche Network: An Experimental Study” and implements the full workflow required to design, execute, analyze, verify, and reproduce the experiment. The primary performance metric is T_visible, defined as the elapsed time between transmission of a signed blockchain transaction and the first successful retrieval of the accepted and updated state from an independent read node. Unlike conventional measurements based only on block interval or transaction receipt latency, this metric captures the complete operational path, including transaction submission, network propagation, block inclusion, consensus acceptance, execution, state commitment, and confirmed read-back. The experimental protocol evaluates five block-production profiles across three network topologies and five offered-load levels using a randomized, paired design with repeated trials. The full registered campaign comprises 750 experimental runs and approximately 34.9 million scheduled transactions.
